title: Structured water molecules drive activation and G protein selectivity in the GPR174 receptor
experiments_summary: 1. G protein coupling profiling: NanoBiT G-protein dissociation assays (NanoLuc Binary Technology) were used in HEK293T cells to quantify LysoPS-induced engagement of Gs, Gi, Gq, and G13 by GPR174, with dose-response curves fitted in GraphPad Prism. 2. Cryo-EM structure determination: GPR174-Gs (2.0 Å) and GPR174-Gi (3.4 Å) complexes were assembled using a NanoBiT tethering strategy in Sf9 insect cells via the Bac-to-Bac baculovirus system with dominant-negative Gα subunits, LysoPS ligand, and stabilizing antibody fragments (Nb35, scFv16). Complexes were purified by amylose resin affinity and size-exclusion chromatography, vitrified on holey carbon grids, and imaged on a Titan Krios 300 kV microscope. Data processing used RELION 4.0 and CryoSPARC; model building used UCSF Chimera, Rosetta, Coot, and Phenix. 3. Site-directed mutagenesis and functional assays: Alanine, conservative, and hydrophobic substitutions were introduced at water-coordinating residues (D65N, R116Q, D288A, Y292A, Q68L, S105A, T205V, T208V, N284L) and G protein interface residues (V55F, M58F, R115A/Q, and others). Mutant receptor activity was assessed by NanoBiT Gs and Gi dissociation assays in HEK293T cells. Cell surface expression of WT and mutant GPR174 was quantified by FLAG-tag ELISA to control for expression differences. 4. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations: Four simulation systems were constructed: GPR174-Gs with internal waters retained (GPR174-Gs-Wat), GPR174-Gs with waters removed (GPR174-Gs-rWat), GPR174-Gi (no internal waters), and P2Y1R-Gs. Systems were embedded in asymmetric lipid bilayers (POPC/PSM/cholesterol outer leaflet; POPC/POPE/POPS/cholesterol inner leaflet) using CHARMM-GUI, solvated in TIP3P water with 0.15 M NaCl, and simulated using GROMACS-2019.4 with the CHARMM36m force field. Three independent 1 µs production runs were performed per system. Water residence times, hydrogen-bond lifetimes (calculated with a custom Python script), reoccupation timescales (~50 ns), and Cα RMSD of coordinating residues were analyzed. 5. Cavity volume analysis: parKVFinder was used to define and measure volumes of the conserved water cavity (CWC), junctional water cavity (JWC), and extended water cavity (EWC) in GPR174 and across a panel of class A GPCR active-state structures. 6. Sequence conservation analysis: GPCRdb was used to perform sequence alignments of cavity-shaping residues (positions 2.50, 2.53, 3.39, 7.45, 7.53, 3.50, 5.58, 5.61) across class A GPCRs, quantifying the frequency of physicochemically similar residues at each position. 7. P2Y1R functional validation: cAMP GloSensor assays were performed in HEK293T cells transfected with WT or mutant P2Y1R (at positions structurally equivalent to GPR174 hydration-network residues) stimulated with ADP, to assess conservation of the hydration-linked signaling scaffold. P2Y1R-Gs MD simulations were also performed to assess water occupancy in the EWC.
